AccountOut.description: The signed-in account, as the account itself may see it.
AccountOut.title: AccountOut

ActivityEventOut.description: One timeline entry. User-facing text only (`REQ-ACT-003`).
ActivityEventOut.title: ActivityEventOut

ActivityPage.description:
Events after a sequence number, plus where to resume from.

`next_after` is what the client sends back, so the polling loop never has to
reason about timestamps — and the Phase 3 SSE upgrade resumes from exactly
the same value (implementation plan §6.3).
ActivityPage.title: ActivityPage

ActivityStatus.description: Per-event status in the activity timeline (`REQ-ACT-004 AC-2`).
ActivityStatus.title: ActivityStatus

AskOut.description: The turn pair a question produces.
AskOut.title: AskOut

AuthOut.description: The outcome of signing up or signing in.
AuthOut.title: AuthOut

ClaimOut.description: One assertion, typed, with the sources behind it (`REQ-SYNTH-002..003`).
ClaimOut.title: ClaimOut

ClaimType.description:
Claim taxonomy (`REQ-SYNTH-002`).

The gate in `REQ-EVID-017 AC-1` is scoped to `FACT`, and
`REQ-SYNTH-009` requires assumptions on `FORECAST`, so these two values are
load-bearing rather than descriptive.
ClaimType.title: ClaimType

ConflictCause.description: Why two pieces of evidence disagree (`REQ-EVID-013 AC-1`).
ConflictCause.title: ConflictCause

ConflictOut.description:
Evidence that disagrees, surfaced rather than resolved away.

`REQ-WORK-009`: conflicts are a visible feature of the report, not hidden.
`explanation` is null when nothing in the evidence accounts for the gap,
and `status` then reads `unresolved` — `REQ-EVID-013 AC-3` forbids
inventing a cause, and `REQ-EVID-014` requires saying so plainly.
ConflictOut.title: ConflictOut

ConflictSideOut.description:
One value in a disagreement, with what a reader needs to judge it.

`REQ-EVID-012 AC-3` names the three: the source, its tier, and when it was
read. Showing the values without them would present a disagreement the
reader has no way to weigh.
ConflictSideOut.title: ConflictSideOut

ConflictStatus.description: Whether a conflict was explained or is surfaced unresolved (`REQ-EVID-014`).
ConflictStatus.title: ConflictStatus

CreateResearchResponse.description: 202: the work is accepted, not finished (`REQ-AGENT-008 AC-1`).
CreateResearchResponse.title: CreateResearchResponse

CredentialsIn.description:
An email and password, for signing up or signing in.

Bounds here are only what keeps the request sane. The password rule
itself (`DEC-16`) is checked by the route, so a too-short password gets a
message saying what the rule is rather than a generic validation failure.
CredentialsIn.title: CredentialsIn

EvidenceOut.description:
One piece of evidence behind a claim, as the inspector shows it.

`REQ-EVID-019 AC-1` names what inspection must show, and "the relevant
evidence" is the item the payload did not carry: source, tier and retrieval
time were all reachable through `source_ids`, but the *excerpt* — the words
the source actually printed — existed only in the database.

That excerpt is the whole point of the citation surface. A reader checking
a claim is checking it against what was written, not against a link.
EvidenceOut.title: EvidenceOut

HistoryItemOut.description: One saved research session in the history list (`REQ-AUTH-005 AC-1`).
HistoryItemOut.title: HistoryItemOut

OwnershipClaimOut.description:
What claiming anonymous research moved (`REQ-AUTH-004`). Not to be
confused with `ClaimOut`, an assertion in a report.
OwnershipClaimOut.title: OwnershipClaimOut

ResearchSessionOut.description: The session header the workspace renders around (`REQ-WORK-002`).
ResearchSessionOut.title: ResearchSessionOut

SectionOut.description: A report section and the claims it renders.
SectionOut.title: SectionOut

SessionStateOut.description:
Who this browser is signed in as, if anyone.

A 200 with `account: null` rather than a 401, because "not signed in" is
the ordinary state of most visitors and not an error to log in a console.
SessionStateOut.title: SessionStateOut

SourceCategory.description: Which tool category produced the source (`REQ-TOOL-002..007`).
SourceCategory.title: SourceCategory

SourceOut.description:
Where a claim's evidence came from, and when it was read.

`retrieved_at` is on the wire because `REQ-EVID-004` makes it part of what
the user is entitled to see, not internal bookkeeping.
SourceOut.title: SourceOut

UploadOut.description: One attached file as the intake panel shows it (`REQ-DOC-003`).
UploadOut.title: UploadOut

UploadTicket.description:
Where to PUT the bytes, and until when.

The URL is a short-lived write grant to one key (`DEC-12`). The API never
sees the file: the browser uploads directly, which is implementation plan
§10 and the reason a 25 MB file does not have to fit through a request
handler.
UploadTicket.title: UploadTicket

UploadTicketRequest.description:
Ask for permission to upload one file.

The size is what the *client* says it is. It is checked here so an
oversized file is refused before it is transferred rather than after
(`REQ-DOC-010 AC-2`), and checked again at completion against the object
that actually arrived, because a declared size is not a limit.
UploadTicketRequest.title: UploadTicketRequest

VersionOut.description: One whole version, in one response.
VersionOut.title: VersionOut

VersionSummary.description: One entry in the version list (`REQ-VER-008`).
VersionSummary.title: VersionSummary

VisualizationOut.description: A chart or table, as a spec the client renders (`DEC-11`).
VisualizationOut.title: VisualizationOut

get.description:
Liveness only. Deliberately does not touch the database: a health
check that fails when Postgres blips takes the API down with it.
Who this browser is signed in as. Never a 401.

post.description: Sign in, and bring this browser's anonymous research into the account.

Revoke this browser's account session. Idempotent.

Revoked in the database, not only cleared in the browser: a copy of the
cookie taken before sign-out must stop working too.
Create an account, sign this browser in, and bring its research along.

get.description: The account's research, most recently updated first.

schema.title: Response List History V1 Me Research Get

post.description:
Start research. **202**, because the answer does not exist yet.

The response is committed rows and nothing else: the run is picked up by
whatever is polling `run_steps`, which is what keeps `OPEN-03` a hosting
question (implementation plan §5.6).

Attach this browser's anonymous research to the signed-in account.

For a visitor who researched while signed out and is already signed in on
this browser. Needs both halves: an account to receive, and an anonymous
session to give. With no anonymous session it moves nothing and says so.

delete.description:
Delete research and everything produced for it (`REQ-SEC-008`, `DEC-18`).

Hidden and stopped in this request, its files removed from storage, and its
rows purged by the worker's sweep once no step can still be writing them.

**Idempotent, and silent about what it could not find.** Research that is
already gone and research that was never this caller's both answer 204:
a 404 for one and not the other would let a guessed id be tested for
existence (`REQ-SEC-009`).

get.description: The session header the workspace renders around (`REQ-WORK-002`).

Events newer than `after` (`REQ-ACT-001`, implementation plan §6.3).

Phase 1 ships polling. Phase 3 gives this same route a streaming content
type; because `seq` is already the resume key, that changes no schema, no
route and no client state model.

The conversation so far (`REQ-CONV-007 AC-2`).

Ownership-scoped like everything else: a conversation is about someone's
research and `REQ-SEC-002` does not stop applying because the surface is a
chat.

schema.title: Response Get Messages V1 Research  Session Id  Messages Get

post.description:
Ask a follow-up, and answer it from the research (`REQ-CONV-001`).

Answered synchronously, unlike a research run. A question against evidence
already gathered is one model call, and pushing it through `run_steps`
would make the reader wait on a poll for something that takes a second.

**Follow-up research is the exception, and it is deliberately not done
here.** `REQ-CONV-003` requires fresh retrieval when the evidence is
insufficient, and retrieval belongs to the pipeline — it needs the budget,
the tool registry, the termination gate and the activity stream, none of
which a request handler should own. So the intent is classified, the answer
says plainly that new research is needed, and enqueuing that run is the
next piece of work. Answering "I researched that" without having done so
would be the one thing this product must never do.

Enqueue the run for a session created with `defer_start`.

**Idempotent.** A session that already has a run is returned unchanged
rather than given a second one: this is the call a client retries after a
dropped connection, and two runs against one version would produce two sets
of claims in the same report.

get.description:
Every file attached to this session, with its processing state.

This is what `REQ-DOC-003 AC-1` is rendered from. Polled by the intake
panel while anything is still processing, which is why it is cheap: one
indexed query and a count per row.

schema.title: Response List Uploads V1 Research  Session Id  Uploads Get

post.description:
Reserve a slot and sign a URL for one file.

**201, not 200**: this creates the `uploads` row. The row exists before the
bytes do, which is what lets the count limit hold — a client that presigns
ten tickets and uploads none has used its ten.

delete.description:
Remove a file and its extracted text (`REQ-SEC-008 AC-2`).

The chunks go with the row, immediately: they are the searchable copy, and
a deleted document that can still be retrieved as evidence is not deleted.
The object is removed next. If storage refuses, the row still goes — the
user's instruction is honoured and the orphaned object is a cleanup
problem, not a privacy one that waits on a retry.

post.description:
Confirm the bytes arrived, and queue the file for reading.

The size is read back from storage and re-checked, which is the second half
of `REQ-DOC-010 AC-1`. A file that is over the limit — or that never
arrived — leaves no usable row behind.

get.description: One version, denormalised into a single response (`NFR-PERF-004`).
